rubrics.justification: The response failed to use the provided Gardner score of 2BB and instead stated morphology was unavailable, then discussed hypothetical higher-grade embryos rather than the actual embryo.

It integrated most relevant patient factors well, including age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor, sperm, BMI, endometrium, and lifestyle, though it did not connect these specifically to the actual 2BB embryo quality.

The reasoning is generally structured, but it is undermined by ignoring the provided embryo grade and basing prognosis on assumed good-quality embryos, making the probability estimate less well supported for this case.

Recommendations such as single embryo transfer, luteal support, and cautious use of PGT-A are broadly guideline-consistent, though omission of the actual 2BB grading limits full alignment with Gardner-based embryo assessment.
It provides practical transfer and future-planning recommendations, but they are somewhat generic and not tailored to the actual 2BB Day 5 blastocyst.
